rules.statement: The petitioner must provide sufficient evidence to resolve doubts and convince the court that the last will was executed freely and willingly.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) The petitioner has failed to lead evidence to remove the doubts and suspicion that have arisen in the mind of the Trial Judge to satisfy his conscience that the Last Will was the act and deed of a free and willful executrix. (2) It is the duty of the propounder of the Last Will to have led evidence to remove doubts and suspicions that arose in evidence. (3) The evidence of the Proctor who prepared the Will is not conclusive as to the mental capacity of the testator. (4) The Judge when he considers the mental condition of the testatrix at the time she signed the Will must put himself the question "Whether the mental faculties of the testator retained sufficient strength fully to comprehend her testamentary act about to be done"
